column2: (3) If such person forcibly resists the endeavour to arrest

column1: him or attempts to evade the arrest, the officer making the

column2: (4) If the officer making the arrest has reasons to believe

column1: that any person to be arrested has entered into or is within
any place, the person residing in or in charge of such place
shall on demand of such officer allow him free ingress therein
and afford all reasonable facilities for a search therein.

column2: (5) If ingress to such place cannot be obtained under the

column1: preceding  subsection  it  shall  be  lawful  in  any  case  for  the

may  issue  but  cannot  be  obtained  without  affording  the
person to be arrested an opportunity of escape, for the officer
to enter such place and search therein.

column2: (6) The officer may break open any outer or inner door or

column1: window of any place in order to liberate himself or any other
person  who,  having  lawfully  entered  for  the  purpose  of
making an arrest, is detained therein.

column2: (7)  The  person  arrested  shall  not  be  subjected  to  more

column1: restraint than is necessary to prevent his escape.

column2: (8) Anything in this section shall not be held to interfere

column1: with or modify the operation of any enactment empowering
an officer to arrest without a warrant.
